summary: American serial con man Napoleon Hill ran lumber, fake-college and charity scams in the early 1900s, abused his family, then invented a meeting with Andrew Carnegie to sell the success books, including Think and Grow Rich, that founded modern self-help.

evidence.note: biography starts with his 1883 birth in rural Wise County, Virginia
1907 move to Mobile to start a timber company that turns out to be a credit-fraud scheme
Automobile College of Washington: students pay to build cars, later a recruitment pyramid
first wife's divorce filing alleges violence, threats and choking of their small daughter
refuses to let his deaf son learn sign language, talking into his skull for hours
pitches The Law of Success built on an invented 1908 meeting with Andrew Carnegie
writes Think and Grow Rich with new wife Rosa Lee, who edits it into a bestseller
New Thought cult adopts his book as scripture and tries to raise an immortal baby
links Hill to Norman Vincent Peale, Christian libertarianism and prosperity gospel under Trump
dies nearly broke in Greenville, South Carolina, in November 1970

notes: Opening segment on the New Thought movement (Quimby, Eddy, Trine, 1800s) is host background, so it is kept out of covered_span and subjects; it appears in keywords and themes. Primary theme wellness-self-help per the taxonomy example, though most airtime is his scams (fraud-grift). Trump appears via Peale and prosperity gospel legacy, setting reaches_present.
